node.title: Re^3: SIGALRM in perl
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Can we figure out why process received the SIGALRM any specific reason for that?

You might try [man://strace], e.g. strace -e trace=signal,alarm ..., but typically, SIGALRM is arranged by [man://alarm] (in Perl, [doc://alarm]). (Update: Also note that "[doc://sleep] may be internally implemented on your system with [doc://alarm].")

If we handle that signal can we raise an exception and override the default operations.

Yes, by setting a [doc://%SIG] handler as [shmem] [id://1228612|showed above]. But I would recommend first trying to figure out where the signal is coming from in the first place.
